newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FOCUS - Estonia's Hansapank boosts profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Estonia's Hansapank boosts profits.

text.p: The leading bank in the Baltic states, Estonia's Hansapank, on Thursday reported a 57 percent rise in 1996 profits and said it aimed to continue its aggressive expansion in the region.
Hansapank has rapidly emerged as market leader in Estonia and already has a subsidiary in Estonia's neighbour Latvia.
It said it was also planning to move into the southernmost and largest Baltic state, Lithuania.
"We want to boost our activites in Lithuania but we do not know our concrete plans yet," Hansapank chairman Juri Mois told a news conference.
"If it was possible, we would open a subsidiary bank," he added. Hansapank is market leader in Estonia, with 25 percent.
Hansapank had 1996 net non-consolidated profits of 234 million Estonian kroons ($18.3 million) versus 149 million kroons in 1995.
It also forecast that its 1997 non-consolidated profit would be 256 million kroons with group earnings of 320 million kroons.
Its shares dipped on the Tallinn stock exchange, where it is regarded as the leading blue chip, as some traders said the 1997 forecast was disappointing.
It was quoted around 180/181 kroons after closing on Wednesday at 183.30 kroons.
The Baltic banking market has been volatile since the three countries of eight million people quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
Each has suffered a serious banking crisis, Lithuania as recently as the end of 1995.
Estonia, hit by bank problems in 1992, is now viewed as having the most advanced banking sector with a high degree of sophistication.
Hansapank said that it was not interested in the Baltic region alone and was eyeing other former Soviet countries.
Mois said the bank would open a representative office in Ukraine.
The bank's assets rose to 5.54 billion kroons from 3.38 billion kroons and it forecast a gain to 7.8 billion kroons of assets in 1997.
